About.title: About this hub
About.dek: A place to move knowledge from Labs to the company, open to anyone who arrives from the web.
About.purpose: Much of what we learn at Labs stays in conversations, prototypes and internal talks. This hub turns that into articles, radars and catalogs that anyone in the company, or outside it, can read, cite and reuse.
About.authorBio: Danilo do Amaral, Design Engineer and AI Builder at Labs. I design and build prototypes, internal tools and AI agents. I present what I learn at our internal tech talks and write it down here.
About.how: Comment on the presentations, send tools for the radar or propose an article. Content marked as draft is open for review.
About.license: State of Prototyping Spring 2026 data belongs to UX Tools, under CC BY 4.0. The texts in this hub are by Danilo do Amaral.

SkillsCli.title: CLI
SkillsCli.dek: Browse and fetch catalogue skills from your terminal. Reads the same registry as the page and the MCP server.
SkillsCli.noDeps: One JavaScript file, zero dependencies. It installs no framework to print a markdown file.
SkillsCli.attributionBody: `get` returns the markdown with the author and licence attached. For the {hosted} hosted ones the content comes from here; for the other {pointer} the command returns the card and the source address, because without a declared licence only the author may redistribute.

SkillsMcp.title: MCP
SkillsMcp.dek: Connect agents to the catalogue over Model Context Protocol. The server exposes the same registry as the CLI.
SkillsMcp.connectBody: HTTP transport, no authentication. In Claude Code, add this to your MCP configuration file:
SkillsMcp.listSkills: Lists the catalogue skills. Takes a free-text filter and a topic. Each item carries author and licence, not just name and description.
SkillsMcp.getSkill: Fetches a skill's markdown by name, slug or author/slug. When a name exists under more than one author, it returns the options instead of choosing for you.
SkillsMcp.provenanceBody: The {hosted} hosted ones come back with the text and the attribution. The other {pointer} come back with the card and the source address: without a declared licence, serving the text would mean redistributing what is not ours.
